clues.text: This city is a capital in far north Canada. It sits on both shores of a long, wide river.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside northern Canada

source.quote: Whitehorse's downtown and Riverdale areas occupy both shores of the Yukon River, which rises in British Columbia and meets the Bering Sea in Alaska.

clues.text: Its spot in a valley helps keep its weather mild. Being near the Pacific also helps soften the cold.
clues.narrowing: narrows to mild-weather spots in the far north

source.quote: Because of the city's location in the Whitehorse valley and relative proximity to the Pacific Ocean, the climate tends to be milder.

clues.text: This place became a city in nineteen fifty. It sits on the long road that leads to Alaska.
clues.narrowing: rules out older northern capitals not on that road

source.quote: It was incorporated in 1950 and is located at kilometre 1426 (Historic Mile 918) on the Alaska Highway in southern Yukon.

clues.text: In summer, the days here grow very long. Light can last for up to nineteen hours a day.
clues.narrowing: narrows to high-latitude places with extreme summer daylight

source.quote: At this latitude, winter days are short and summer days have up to about 19 hours of daylight.

clues.text: Yukon's seat of government stands here. Its folk count tops each town across the top of this land.
clues.narrowing: confirms the Yukon capital as the only candidate

source.quote: Whitehorse is the capital of Yukon, and the largest city in Northern Canada.
